label: theoremA
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{theoremA}
There exists $L_0 >0$ so that for all $L \geq L_0$ the inf spectrum satisfies 
\[
A \frac{e^{L}}{2L} \leq \# \bigl\{[\gamma] \mid m_{[\gamma]} \leq L \bigr\} \leq Be^{C L}
\]
where $A,B$ and $C$ are constants which only depend on $g$. 
The constant $A$ can be taken to be
$$
A= \frac{1}{6} \left( g+ \floor*{\frac{g^2+3}{12}}\right).
$$
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
(Proposition \ref{prop: thickened metric})
For $\gamma$ a closed curve with $i(\gamma,\gamma)=n$, there exists a metric $Y_{\gamma}$ such that $\ell_{\gamma}(Y_{\gamma})\leq c\, m_{\gamma}$ where ${\rm sys}(Y_\gamma)\geq \frac{1}{5n}$. The constant $c \geq 1$ depends only on the topology of $X$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The following items give a brief condensed description of some of the ancillary results that arise in the investigation of the inf spectrum properties and in the proof of Theorem \ref{theoremA}. More details can be found in 
Sections \ref{sec:inf}, \ref{section:counting figure 8's}, and \ref{sec:propertiesofinfspec}.
\begin{itemize} 
 \item {\bf The constants.}
 The constant $A$ is the number of $\mathrm{Mod}_{g}$ orbits of punctured tori (there is only one) and embedded pairs of pants. See Proposition \ref{prop: infspecproperties}.
The constants $B$ and $C$ can be upper bounded using the final estimates in the proof of Theorem \ref{theoremA}. 

\item {\bf Multiplicity.} The first number  in  the inf spectrum, $0$,    has multiplicity 
$\floor{\frac{g}{2}}+1$, this is the number of $\mathrm{Mod}_g$ orbits of essential simple closed curves. Next is $2{\,\rm arccosh} (3)$ with multiplicity 
\begin{equation}
 2g-2+\floor*{\frac{(g-1)^2}{4}}.
 \end{equation}
This is the number of 
$\mathrm{Mod}_g$ orbits of figure $8$s on the surface. This multiplicity determines the genus of the surface. See Proposition \ref{enum: counting}.

\item {\bf Curve types and inf length.} While there is very little one can surmise about the curve type of a length that appears in the length spectrum, for the inf spectrum there are a number of interesting 
conclusions one can draw knowing the inf length. See Section \ref{sec:propertiesofinfspec}.

\item {\bf Length spectrum comparison.} Comparing the length spectrum of a hyperbolic metric $X$ on the closed surface $\Sigma$ to the inf spectrum of $\Sigma$, we see that the lower bound constant in the inf spectrum is larger since $A >1$. In fact, a more germane comparison is with respect to the spectrum of minimal $X$-length representatives in each mapping class orbit which is a strictly smaller set though has the same growth rate as the length spectrum \cite{BP}. 
\end{itemize}
head: environment

label: def:teich
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:teich}
Fix a smooth closed oriented surface $S$ of genus $g \geq 2$. The \emph{Teichm\"uller space}
${\mathcal T}_g$ is the space of isotopy classes of hyperbolic metrics on $S$:
\[
	{\mathcal T}_g \;:=\; \bigl\{\text{hyperbolic metrics on }S\bigr\} \big/ {\sim},
\]
where two metrics are equivalent if they are related by an isometry isotopic to the identity.
A point $X \in {\mathcal T}_g$ is called a \emph{marked hyperbolic surface}.

The \emph{mapping class group} $\mathrm{Mod}_g := \mathrm{Mod}(S)$ is the group of isotopy classes of
orientation-preserving homeomorphisms $S\to S$. It acts on ${\mathcal T}_g$ by re-marking: for
$\phi\in\mathrm{Mod}_g$ and $X\in{\mathcal T}_g$, set $\phi\cdot X := X\circ\phi^{-1}$ (with the induced
metric). The quotient
\[
	{\mathcal M}_g \;:=\; {\mathcal T}_g / \mathrm{Mod}_g
\]
is the \emph{moduli space} of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces; its points are isometry classes
of closed hyperbolic surfaces of genus $g$.
head: environment
name: Teichm\"uller space and moduli space

label: def:FN
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:FN}
A \emph{pants decomposition} of $S$ is a maximal collection
$P = \{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{3g-3}\}$ of isotopy classes of pairwise disjoint, pairwise
non-isotopic simple closed curves. The complement
$S\setminus(\gamma_1\cup\cdots\cup\gamma_{3g-3})$ consists of $2(g-1)$ pairs of pants
(three-holed spheres).

Given a pants decomposition $P$, every marked surface $X\in{\mathcal T}_g$ is completely determined by
its \emph{Fenchel--Nielsen coordinates}
\[
	\bigl(\ell_{\gamma_1}(X),\ldots,\ell_{\gamma_{3g-3}}(X);\;
	\tau_{\gamma_1}(X),\ldots,\tau_{\gamma_{3g-3}}(X)\bigr)
	\;\in\; {\mathbb R}_{>0}^{3g-3}\times{\mathbb R}^{3g-3},
\]
where $\ell_{\gamma_i}(X)>0$ is the hyperbolic length of the geodesic representative of
$\gamma_i$ in $X$, and $\tau_{\gamma_i}(X)\in{\mathbb R}$ is the corresponding twist parameter.
The Fenchel--Nielsen map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism
${\mathcal T}_g \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}{\mathbb R}_{>0}^{3g-3}\times{\mathbb R}^{3g-3}$.
head: environment
name: Fenchel--Nielsen coordinates

label: def:length
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:length}
Every free homotopy class of essential closed curves on $X$ contains a unique closed geodesic
representative. For a closed curve $\gamma$, we write $\ell_\gamma(X)$ for the hyperbolic
length of its geodesic representative on $X$. The function
$\ell_\gamma\colon{\mathcal T}_g\to{\mathbb R}_{>0}$ is real-analytic.

The \emph{systole} of $X$ is
\[
	{\rm sys}(X) \;:=\; \min_\gamma \ell_\gamma(X),
\]
the minimum taken over all (free homotopy classes of) essential closed curves. For
$\varepsilon>0$, the \emph{$\varepsilon$-thick part} of moduli space is
\[
	{\mathcal M}_g^\varepsilon \;:=\; \bigl\{X\in{\mathcal M}_g : {\rm sys}(X)\geq\varepsilon\bigr\}.
\]
head: environment
name: Curve lengths and systole

label: thm:Bers
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Bers}
For each $g \geq 2$, there exists a constant $B_{g}$ so that any hyperbolic surface $X$ of genus $g$ has a pants decomposition whose pants curves have length less than $B_{g}$. Moreover, the decomposition can be chosen to include all curves of length at most $1$ on $X$.
head: environment

label: lem:WolpertLemma
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:WolpertLemma}
Suppose $\phi : X \rightarrow Y$ is a K-quasiconformal homeomorphism between two hyperbolic surfaces. Then
$$
\frac{\ell_{\gamma}(X)}{K} \leq \ell_{\phi(\gamma)}(Y) \leq K \ell_{\gamma}(X)
$$
for any closed curve $\gamma$ on $X$.

label: lem:bishop
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:bishop}
If two pairs of pants have an upper bound on their pants curves, and an upper bound on the ratios of lengths between their boundary curves, then there is a quasiconformal mapping between them with a constant that only depends on these two bounds. Moreover, the quasiconformal homeomorphism can be chosen so that it is affine on the boundary geodesics.

label: rem:embedding
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:embedding}
While we focus on the moduli space ${\mathcal M}_g$ of closed surfaces of genus $g$, the moduli space of complete finite area of surfaces of finite-type can be embedded in the closure $\overline{{\mathcal M}_g}$ for a well chosen $g$. Specifically, the moduli space of a genus $h$ surface with $m$ cusps can be embedded in $\overline{{\mathcal M}_g}$ where $g=h +\lceil\frac{m}{2}\rceil$. It follows that our upper bounds on the growth of the inf spectrum for ${\mathcal M}_{h,m}$ are direct consequences of our upper bounds for ${\mathcal M}_g$.
head: environment

title: Notation
body_md:
Fix $a,b >0$ and let $P_x$ be a pair of pants with cuffs of length $a$, $b$ and a cuff $\alpha$ of length $x$ where $0 \leq x \leq 1$. 
 Denote by $\mathcal{H}_x \subset P_{x}$ the half-collar bounded by an equidistant curve of length $1$ and the geodesic of length $x$, $0 \leq x \leq 1$. 
 Next for $x<t \leq 1$, denote the equidistant neighborhood of boundary length $t$ deleted from $\mathcal{H}_x$ by $\mathcal{H}_{x}^t \subset \mathcal{H}_x$. Finally, denote by $P_{x}^{1}$ the pair of pants $P_x$ with $\mathcal{H}_x$ deleted; that is,
 $P_{x}^{1}$ is the pair of pants with the collar neighborhood about $\alpha$ of boundary length 1 deleted.
head: manual

label: lem:geomcollars
title: Lemma
body_md:
(Type I) \label{lem:geomcollars}
The hyperbolic cylinders $\mathcal{H}_{x}^{t}$ and $\mathcal{H}_0^t$ are $C_x$-biLipschitz equivalent by a mapping which when restricted to either boundary curve is an isometry. 
If $0 \leq x,y <t \leq 1$, then the total length of the arcs of type I in $\mathcal{H}_{x}^{t}$ is not increased by more than a multiplicative factor of $C_1^2$
by a biLipschitz mapping $\phi : \mathcal{H}_{x}^{t} \rightarrow \mathcal{H}_{y}^{t}$ which when restricted to the boundary 
of $\mathcal{H}_{x}^{t}$ is an isometry.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As $x$ goes to $0$, there is geometric convergence of $\mathcal{H}_x$ to $\mathcal{H}_0$. Restricting to the truncated compact regions 
 $\mathcal{H}_{x}^{t}$ and $\mathcal{H}_0^t$ implies the result (see Proposition \ref{prop: geometricconvergence}). 
 Since the total self-intersection of $\gamma$ is $n$, the arcs of type I remain in the truncated part of the cusp collar
 (see for instance \cite{basmajian2025primeorthogeodesics}), say in $\mathcal{H}_0^t$, for some $t>0$ that is a function of $n$. Using the bi-Lipschitz equivalence twice,
 first from $\mathcal{H}_x^t$ to $\mathcal{H}_0^t$, and then from $\mathcal{H}_0^t$ to $\mathcal{H}_y^t$ we have that 
 $\mathcal{H}_x^t$ is $C_{x}C_{y}$-biLipschitz equivalent to $\mathcal{H}_y^t$. Finally, $C_{x}C_{y} \leq C_1^2$ yields the result.
head: environment

label: lem:geompants
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:geompants}
 For all $x$ where $0 \leq x \leq 1$, $P_x^1$ and $P_0^1$ are $D_x$-biLipschitz equivalent by a biLipschitz map that is an isometry on the boundary curves. If $0 \leq x,y \leq 1$, then the total length of the arcs of type II in $P_x^1$ is not increased by more than a multiplicative factor of $D_1^2$ by a biLipschitz mapping $\psi: \mathcal{P}_{x}^{1} \rightarrow \mathcal{P}_{y}^{1}$ which when restricted to the boundary of $\mathcal{P}_{x}^{1}$ is an isometry.
head: environment
name: Type II

title: Proof
body_md:
As $x$ goes to $0$, $P_x$ geometrically converges to $P_0$. Now restricting to the compact regions $P_x^1$ and $P_0^1$ implies the desired biLipschitz equivalence, see Proposition \ref{prop: geometricconvergence}. By composing the biLipschitz map from $P_{x}^{1}$ to $P_{0}^1$ with the biLipschitz map from $P_{0}^1$ to $P^{1}_{y}$, we obtain a biLipschitz map from $P_{x}^{1}$ to $P^{1}_{y}$
with constant $D_{x} D_{y}$ and the result follows.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $X$ be a closed hyperbolic surface and $\alpha$ a simple closed geodesic of length $x$ and $s$ a geodesic arc that enters and leaves the collar $\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(x)$. Then the {\it geometric winding of $s$ about $\alpha$}

$$
gw_{\alpha}(s):=\biggl\lfloor \frac{L}{\ell_{\alpha}(X)} \biggr\rfloor
$$
where $L$ is the length of the orthogonal projection of $s$ onto $\alpha$.
head: environment

label: lem: typeIII
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $m=|\mathcal{A}|=|\mathcal{A}^{\prime}|$ be the number of strands. 
If $m=0$ then there is nothing to prove. If $m=1$, then Wolpert's 
infinitesimal twist formula (see \cite{BuserBook}) dictates that the single strand that passes through $\alpha$ must intersect $\alpha$ at a right angle with respect to the 
optimal metric $X_{\gamma}$. 

Next, suppose there are $m \geq 2$ strands. First note that without loss of generality we can assume (by Dehn twisting) that one of the strands has geometric winding number about $\alpha$ being 0. That is, the strand makes less than a full turn about 
$\alpha$. Now, since the self-intersection number of $\gamma$ is $n$ the sum

\begin{equation}\label{eq: sum}
\sum_{s^{\prime} \in \mathcal{A}^{\prime}} \text{gw}_{\alpha}(s^{\prime}) \leq n.
\end{equation}

Recall that the collar width of $\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(\frac{1}{n})$ is 
$2 {\,\rm arccosh} \left( n \right) \leq 2 \log n +2\log 2$. Now note that an arc $s^{\prime} \in \mathcal{A}^{\prime}$ which traverses the collar can be upper bounded by twice the width of the collar plus 
$g\text{}w_{\alpha}(s^{\prime}) (\frac{1}{n})$ plus $\frac{1}{2}$ to allow for traversing boundary. That is, a piecewise geodesic comprised of an orthogeodesic segment, followed by traversing the geodesic 
$\alpha$ a $ \text{gw}_{\alpha}(s^{\prime})$ number of times, followed by another orthogeodesic segment, and finally an arc of length less than $\frac{1}{2}$ along the length one boundary. This yields


\begin{equation}
\ell_{s^{\prime}}\left(\frac{1}{n}\right) 
\leq 2 \log n +2 \log 2 + \text{gw}_{\alpha}(s^{\prime})\cdot \frac{1}{n} +\frac{1}{2}.
\end{equation}

Using inequality (\ref{eq: sum}) and summing over the geodesic arcs we have


\begin{align}
\sum_{s^{\prime} \in \mathcal{A}^{\prime}}\ell_{s^{\prime}}\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)
&\leq 2m \log n + 2m \log 2 + 1 +\frac{m}{2} = 2m \log n + m \left(2\log 2 +\frac{1}{2}\right)+ 1 \\
\label{eq:upperbound} &\leq 2m \log n + 2m+ 1 \leq 2m\log n + 2m \log 5 =2m \log 5n \\
& \leq 2m {\,\rm arccosh} \left(5n \right) = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{A}} 2 {\,\rm arccosh} \left(5n \right) \leq \sum_{s \in S} \ell_{s}\left(\frac{1}{5n} \right) \\
&\leq \sum_{s \in \mathcal{A}} \ell_{s}\left(x \right)
\end{align}

In the second inequality of expression (\ref{eq:upperbound}) we have used the fact that $m \geq 2$.
The next to last inequality follows from the fact that a strand in $X$ passing through the collar must have length at least 
 the width of the collar which is $2 {\,\rm arccosh} \left(5n \right)$. Finally, the last inequality follows from our assumption that 
 $x \leq \frac{1}{5n}$.
head: environment

label: lem:strict
title: Lemma
body_md:
(local surgery)\label{lem:strict} Suppose $X$ is a hyperbolic surface with a short pants decomposition 
 having a pants curve $\alpha$ of length less than $\frac{1}{5n}$. Then the metric $Y$ with all Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates the same as that for $X$ except for the $\alpha$ curve for which $\ell_{\alpha}(Y)=\frac{1}{n}$
satisfies 
\begin{equation}
 \ell_{\gamma}(Y)\leq C\ \ell_{\gamma}(X) \text{, for any curve $\gamma$ with $i(\gamma, \gamma)=n$}.
\end{equation}
The constant $C \geq 1$ depends only on the topology of $X$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\gamma \subset X$ have intersection number $n$, and suppose the curve $\alpha$ bounds the pairs of pants $P$ and 
$Q$. Let $X^{\prime}$, resp. $Y^{\prime}$, be the geometry of $X$, resp. $Y$, outside $P \cup Q$. By assumption
$X^{\prime}=Y^{\prime}$, and hence $\ell_{\gamma}(X^{\prime})=\ell_{\gamma}(Y^{\prime})$. As a result, we need only focus on the $\gamma$ arcs in $P \cup Q$. Moreover, since arcs of type I or II are contained in one of the pants $P$ or $Q$, we will argue on the pair of pants $P$, the same holds for the type I or II arcs on $Q$.

 
 

Arcs of type I are controlled by Lemma \ref{lem:geomcollars}. There is a $C$-biLipschitz map $\phi : H_{x}^{t} \rightarrow H_{\frac{1}{n}}^t$ which is an isometry on the length 1 boundary curve. Here $t$ is a function of $n$. If $s$ is such an arc
then the biLipschitz image $\phi (s)$ has the same relative position on the boundary of length 1 as $s$ does. 




Arcs of type II are controlled by Lemma \ref{lem:geompants}. There is a $C$-biLipschitz map $\psi : P_{x}^{1} \rightarrow P_{\frac{1}{n}}^1$ which is an isometry on the boundary of $P_{x}^{1}$. If $s$ is such an arc, then $\psi (s)$ has the same relative position on the boundary of $P_{x}^{1}$ as $s$ does. Here, the biLipschitz constant depends on the lengths of the other two boundary geodesics of the pair of pants $P$. Thus, the biLipschitz constant may be different for $Q$, but we will take the larger of the two. In the end, it will not matter since all the pants curves have length bounded above by the Bers constant. 

The union of the type III arcs is the set $\gamma \cap \mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(x)$. For each type III arc $s$ in $\gamma \cap \mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(x)$, we construct a geodesic arc 
$s^{\prime} \in \mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(\frac{1}{n})$ that starts and ends at the same boundary points as $s$ did, and which has the same geometric winding number around $\alpha$ as $s$ does. By Lemma \ref{lem: typeIII} we have
\begin{equation}
\sum_{s^{\prime} \in \gamma \cap \mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(\frac{1}{n})} \ell_{s^{\prime}} \left(\frac{1}{n}\right)
\leq \sum_{s \in \gamma \cap \mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(x)} \ell_{s}\left(x \right).
\end{equation}


We now build a curve $\gamma^{\prime} \subset Y$ in the same homotopy class as $\gamma$. Outside of the two pairs of pants 
that bound $\alpha$, we let $\gamma^{\prime}=\gamma$. Hence, $\ell_{\gamma^{\prime}}(Y^{\prime})=\ell_{\gamma}(X^{\prime})$.



Choose an orientation on the geodesic $\gamma \subset X$ and an initial point. Then $\gamma$ decomposes into a
 union of ordered geodesic arcs $s_{1}, s_{2},..., s_{m}$ in $X$; that is,
 $\gamma = s_{1}*s_{2}*...*s_{m}$
 where an arc $s_{i}$ is either a connected segment of $\gamma$ in $X-\{PUQ \}$, a type I arc in $P$ (or in $Q$),
 a type II arc in $P$ (or in $Q$), or a type III arc in $P \cup Q$.

 We next define a curve $\gamma^{\prime} \subset Y$ using the biLipschitz mappings $\phi$ and $\psi$ above. 

 Define

\begin{equation}
\Phi (s_{i})= 
\begin{cases}
 s_{i} , \text{ if } s_{i} \subset X^{\prime}\\
 \phi (s_i), \text{ if } s_{i} \text{ is type I in } P \cup Q \\
 \psi (s_i), \text{ if } s_{i} \text{ is type II in } P \cup Q \\
 s_{i}^{\prime}, \text{ if } s_{i} \text{ is type III in } P \cup Q 
\end{cases}
\end{equation}

 
Then our curve in $Y$ is 

\begin{equation}
 \Phi (\gamma)=\Phi(s_{1})*\Phi(s_{2})*...*\Phi(s_{m}) 
\end{equation}


Since the biLipshitz mapping $\phi$ respects the relative position of a point on the boundary of the truncated half-collar 
and $\psi$ respects the relative position of a point on the boundary of the truncated pair of pants, our constructed curve 
$\Phi (\gamma)$ is continuous and in the same homotopy class as $\gamma$. Moreover, by construction, at worst $\Phi$ increases the length of an arc by the maximum of the two biLipshitz constants. Thus we have





\begin{equation}
\ell_{\gamma}(Y)\leq 
\sum_{i=1}^{m} \ell_{\Phi(s_{i})}(Y)
\leq C \sum_{i=1}^{m} \ell_{s_{i}}(X)
=C \ell_{\gamma}(X)
\end{equation}
The first inequality is from the fact that the $Y$-length of the geodesic in the homotopy class of $\gamma$ is at most 
the $Y$-length of $\Phi (\gamma)$. Finally, the constant $C \geq 1$ depends only on the topology of $X$.
head: environment

label: prop: thickened metric
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: thickened metric}
For $\gamma$ a closed curve with $i(\gamma,\gamma)=n$, there exists a metric $Y_{\gamma}$ such that $\ell_{\gamma}(Y_{\gamma})\leq c\, m_{\gamma}$ where ${\rm sys}(Y_\gamma)\geq \frac{1}{5n}$. The constant $c \geq 1$ depends only on the topology of $X$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\gamma$ be a closed curve with $i(\gamma,\gamma)=n$. 
By the collar lemma, there are at most $3g-3$ curves of length less than $\frac{1}{5n}$ on $X_{\gamma}$ which we denote as 
$\alpha_1,\alpha_2,..., \alpha_m$; $0 \leq m \leq 3g-3$. Take a short pants decomposition which necessarily includes these curves. Using Lemma \ref{lem:strict}, we perform surgery on $\alpha_1$ to obtain the metric $Y_1$ which has 
$\ell_{\alpha_1} (Y_1)=\frac{1}{n}$ and the geometry in the complement of the pants containing $\alpha_1$ being unchanged. In particular, the lengths of the other pants curves remain the same. We continue by performing this surgery on $\alpha_2$, to obtain $Y_2$ and continue $m$-times to achieve the final metric $Y_{\gamma}$ with ${\rm sys} (Y_{\gamma}) \geq \frac{1}{5n}.$ 
If the surgered curves do not bound the same pair of pants in the short decomposition then their respective bilipschitz maps are independent of each other, and the multiplicative constant $C$ in Lemma \ref{lem:strict} remains the same. Since there are at most 3 surgered curves that can bound a pair of pants, the multiplicative constant is at most 
$C^3$ (where $C$ is the constant from Lemma \ref{lem:strict}), and we conclude that 
$\ell_{\gamma}(Y_{\gamma})\leq C^{3} \ell_{\gamma}(X_{\gamma})= C^{3} m_{\gamma}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: We note here that $c=C^3$, where $C$ is the constant in Lemma \ref{lem:strict}.
head: environment

label: lem: model metric properties
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: model metric properties}
Let $\mathbf{M}_g$ be the set of all model metrics, and $Z^{P}_{\vec{k}}$ be a model metric associated to the pants decomposition
$P$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If all the coordinates of $\vec{k}$ are non-zero, then the model metric $Z^{P}_{\vec{k}}$ is contained in ${\mathcal M}_g^{1/5n}$
\item If a coordinate of $\vec{k}$ is zero, then $Z^{P}_{\vec{k}}$ is a surface with nodes on the boundary of ${\mathcal M}_g$. Moreover, the number of such zeros correspond to the number of nodes on the hyperbolic surface. 

\item The number of mapping class group orbits of pants decompositions for a genus $g \geq 2$ surface, denoted $t_{g}$, only depends on the 
topology of the surface. Moreover, $t_g$ is the number of trivalent graphs with 
exactly $2g-2$ vertices. 



\item \label{item: modelmetricnumber} the number of model metrics in 
$\mathbf{M}_g^{n}$ is $t_{g} (n+1)^{(3g-3)}$.

\item \label{item: qc constant} There exists a constant $Q_g$, which only depends on $g$, such that any surface in ${\mathcal M}_g^{1/5n}$ is $Q_g$-quasiconformally equivalent to a model metric in $\mathbf{M}_g^n$. 
Similarly, any metric in the $\frac{1}{5n}$-thick part of the boundary of ${\mathcal M}_g$ is $Q_g$-quasiconformally equivalent to a model metric in $\mathbf{M}_g^{n}$.

\item any metric in $\mathbf{M}_g^{n-1}$ is $Q_g$-quasiconformally equivalent to some model metric in $\mathbf{M}_g^{n}$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Model metric properties

title: Proof
body_md:
To prove item (1) need to show that the systole of $Z^{P}_{\vec{k}}$ is $\geq \frac{1}{5n}$. Suppose not. 
Since the pants curves are bounded from above $B_{g}$, the systole cannot cross a pants curve and have length less than $\frac{1}{5n}$. This only leaves that the systole is a pants curve but by assumption all the pants curves have length a positive integer multiple of $\frac{1}{n}$. Thus it must be that the systole is bigger than $\frac{1}{5n}$. Item (2) follows from the definitions. 

To prove item (3), we first note that a pants decomposition can be identified 
with a $3$-regular graph with $2g-2$ vertices by putting a vertex for each pair of pants and connecting two vertices with an edge if they share a pants curve. 
Moreover, this correspondence uniquely identifies the mapping class orbit of the 
pants decomposition. Hence, the number of pants decomposition orbits is the number of trivalent graphs, $t_g$.
 
 Item (4) follows from the fact that there are $t_g$ pants decompositions up to an element of the mapping class group, and the number of 
 possible values for the length of any pants curve is $(n+1)^{3g-3}$.

To prove item (5), note that by Theorem \ref{thm:Bers} any surface $X \in {\mathcal M}_g^{1/5n}$ admits a pants decomposition
$P=\{\alpha_1,...,\alpha_{3g-3} \}$ with length upper bounded by $B_g$ and which contains all curves of length less than $2{\,\rm arcsinh}(1)$. We need to find an appropriate model metric with respect to $P$. This of course comes down 
to an appropriate choice of the vector $\vec{k}$.


Now if $\ell_{\alpha_{i}}(X) \in I$, where $I$ is one of the following intervals
\begin{equation*}
 \left[ \frac{1}{5n},\frac{1}{n} \right], \left(\frac{1}{n}, \frac{2}{n}\right],...,
\left(\frac{k-1}{n}, \frac{k}{n}\right],..., \left(\frac{n-1}{n}, 1 \right].
\end{equation*}
then choose $k_{i}$ so that $\frac{k_{i}}{n}$ is the biggest value in $I$.
Otherwise, $I=[1, B_g]$ and we set $k_{i}=n$ so that the model metric length coordinate is
$\ell_{\alpha_{i}}(Z^{P}_{\vec{k}})=1$.
 Setting all the twist parameters to be zero, this defines a model metric $Z^{P}_{\vec{k}}$. Now,
if $X_0$ has the same length parameters as $X$ but with zero twists, then the pants lengths from 
$Z^{P}_{\vec{k}}$ to $X_{0}$ are multiplied by at most 
$\text{max}\{B_g, 5\}$. Moreover, going from $X_0$ to $X$ involves 
twisting along each $\alpha_i$. Noting that the twists are locally supported about their respective curves, and that this mapping can be realized by a Nielsen twist about each curve with dilatation $K_i$,
for $i=1,...,3g-3$, we can conclude there is a quasiconformal mapping from $X_0$ to $X$ with dilatation bounded 
by the maximum of $\{K_1,...,K_{3g-3}\}$. The dilatations $K_i$ only depend on the upper bound of the length of the curve which is $B_g.$ See \cite{Matsuzaki2007} for a proof of this fact. 
Thus, by a theorem of Bishop (Proposition \ref{prop:bishop}) the map from $Z^{P}_{\vec{k}}$ to $X$ has dilatation at most 
$Q_g=f(\text{max}\{B_g, 5\}, B_g)$. The double function is because 
$\text{max}\{B_g, 5\}$ is  the upper bound on the length ratio and $B_g$ is the  upper bound on the pants lengths. Thus, the dilatation of the map from $Z^{P}_{\vec{k}}$ to $X$ depends only on the genus $g$. The argument for $X$ on the boundary of moduli space is similar and left to the reader. 

Finally, item (6) follows from item (\ref{item: qc constant}) and the fact that a model metric in $\mathbf{M}_g^{n-1}$ lies in the moduli space 
${\mathcal M}_g^{1/5(n-1)} \subset {\mathcal M}_g^{1/5n}$.

body_md: We remark that upper bounds as well as the asymptotic growth rate of $t_g$, as $g \rightarrow \infty$, are known. See Bollab\'as \cite{Bollobas1982}.

title: Proof
body_md:
The fact that there is only one type of punctured torus follows from the fact that the complement of the punctured torus 
must have genus $g-1$ with one boundary component. After cutting along the nonseparating curve of the torus what remains is an embedded pair of pants which has only one figure $8$ up to an element of the mapping class group that keeps the nonseparating curve of the torus invariant. This verifies item (1).

 To prove item (2), note that the curve $\gamma$ deformation retracts onto a figure $8$ in $P$. Since figure $8$s track with the pants they are in we have a similar phenomenon for closed curves in pants.

label: prop: infspecproperties
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: infspecproperties}
 Let $\Sigma$ be a closed surface of genus $g \geq 2$.
\begin{enumerate}

\item The first two numbers in the inf spectrum are $0$ and 
$2{\,\rm arccosh} \, 3$. 

\item The multiplicity of $0$ is the number of mapping class group orbits of simple curves which equals $\floor{\frac{g}{2}} +1$.

\item The multiplicity of 
$2{\,\rm arccosh} \,3$ is the number of mapping class group orbits of figure 8 curves which is
the increasing function 
\begin{equation}
 2g-2+\floor*{\frac{(g-1)^2}{4}}.
 \end{equation}
In particular, the inf spectrum determines the topology of $\Sigma$. 

\item If $\Sigma^{\prime}$ is a subsurface of $\Sigma$ then 
$\mathrm{Inf\,Spec}({\mathcal M}')$ injects into $\mathrm{Inf\,Spec}({\mathcal M})$. 

\item The primitive length spectrum of an ideal pair of pants injects into $\mathrm{Inf\,Spec}({\mathcal M})$. 
In particular:
$$
\{2{\,\rm arccosh} (2k+1)\}_{k=1}^{\infty} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Inf\,Spec}({\mathcal M}).
$$
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The inf length of an essential simple closed curve is $0$, and the figure $8$ being the shortest non-simple curve (\cite{BuserBook}) is guaranteed to be the next shortest inf length. The proof of item (1) is finished by noting that a figure $8$ has inf length equal to $2{\,\rm arccosh} \, 3$. The proof of item (2) is clear. The proof of item (3) follows from Proposition
\ref{enum: counting}. Item (4) follows from the fact that any curve in 
$\Sigma'$ is also a curve in $\Sigma$, and the fact that the inf length of a curve on a subsurface is the same as its inf length on any other surface that contains $\Sigma'$. Finally, item (5) follows from the fact that the inf length of a curve on an embedded pair of pants is exactly the length of that curve on an ideal pair of pants.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: In item (4) of Proposition \ref{prop: infspecproperties} the multiplicity of the inf length of a curve can change depending on the surface it is contained in. For example, the multiplicity of figure $8$s changes in going to a bigger surface.
